posts.text: Yep, we are trying to figure out how best to add decode paths to Quail. Single or two-token projects (e.g., AI.CLASSIFY) are not so bad because they are still compute-bound. Scheduling gets tricky for open-ended AI MAP operators; we need to mix decode into prefill passes (we can try to "hide" decode under document reading). The challenge here is to be able to accurately estimate the length of an AI MAP operator output; so we can plan well

posts.text: 🙏 James!  Loved reconnecting w/you about the historical progression from Jester (1998) to Hot-or-Not (2000) to @Facebook (2004) and @YouTube (2005)…. Go Bears!! @UCBerkeley

quotedTweet.text:
Was thrilled to run into Berkeley Professor @Ken_Goldberg at the Cal Football game (😭), thanks to an invite from @jfiance and @thehousefund . Ken brilliantly launched the Jester project in 1999 which was a pioneer in the concept of collaborative filtering, essentially it was Funny or Not. We obviously took great inspiration from it, the original goal of hot or not was to create a collaborative filtering dataset for dating.  It's just a reminder to me of how important the influence of one's environment can be, to learn from and to build on.  Berkeley was always a place where the kooky fun ideas could blossom, I hope it still is! Thank you Ken!!

https://t.co/LRIYFAHE4d
quotedTweet.translationZh:
在 Cal Football 比赛上遇到 Berkeley 教授 @Ken_Goldberg，我非常激动（😭），感谢 @jfiance 和 @thehousefund 的邀请。Ken 在 1999 年出色地推出了 Jester 项目，这是协同过滤概念的先驱，本质上就是 Funny or Not。我们显然深受其启发，hot or not 最初的目标就是为约会创建一个协同过滤数据集。

这也提醒我，一个人所处环境的影响有多么重要：从中学习，并在其基础上构建。Berkeley 一直是那些古怪有趣想法能够开花结果的地方，希望现在依然如此！谢谢你，Ken！！
